name: Wiring heat budget at the mixing chamber for a 50-qubit superconducting processor
plain_name: Check that the wiring for a superconducting qubit chip does not overheat the coldest stage
description: Krinner et al. engineered the wiring of a 50-qubit processor (50 drive, 50 flux and 8 output lines plus 8 readout-drive lines) and designed it so that the heat load stays at least about three times below the mixing-chamber cooling power. This profile checks that budget on a candidate dilution refrigerator.

sources.citation: Engineering cryogenic setups for 100-qubit scale superconducting circuit systems

reported_conditions.as_printed: heat load at least about a factor three smaller than cooling power

requirements.rationale: The heat budget is evaluated at 20 mK, the temperature at which Krinner et al. quote the mixing-chamber cooling power.
A 50-qubit processor with individual drive and flux control needs 124 RF lines.

params.name: operating_temperature
params.description: Mixing-chamber temperature at which the budget is evaluated

params.name: n_drive_lines
params.description: 50 qubit drive lines + 8 readout drive lines (stainless steel UT-085-SS-SS)

params.name: q_drive_line
params.description: Measured passive load per drive line at the MXC, 0.013(6) µW

params.name: q_flux_line
params.description: Measured passive load per flux line at the MXC, 0.029(5) µW

params.name: q_output_line
params.description: Measured passive load per output line at the MXC, 0.020(16) µW

params.name: p_flux_dc
params.description: Average DC flux-bias dissipation per flux line at the MXC, 0.050(3) µW

params.name: design_margin
params.description: Design rule: heat load at least about three times smaller than the cooling power

coupled.rationale: Krinner et al.'s design rule applied to the documented cooling power of the candidate refrigerator.

missing_information: active drive-line dissipation at operating power (paper estimates it separately)
uncertainties of the per-line loads are not propagated
confirmation_note: Profile author reviewed the requirements on 2026-10-31; users must re-confirm edited values.
